# The solution folder (template, records beside the code)

> A strategic definition of how one or more problems can be addressed to fulfill the intent.

A repository that keeps its records beside the code lists, in `esoi.toml`, the folders that may hold them (`[records] beside_code = ["pkg", "pkg/*"]`). A folder that holds records is a code folder: it keeps the code, the record files of the solutions whose code it holds, and a generated `README.md`. It is not an intent unless it also holds an `intent.csv`. Each record lives once. The standard is [records beside the code](../../reference/records-beside-code.md).

```
<top intent folder>/       the top intent only (esoi by default)
  intent.csv
  README.md                 generated
<code folder>/                  a solution folder: code, records and a generated README
  solutions.csv  implementations.csv  metrics.csv  problems.csv  ideals.csv   only the files it has rows for
  README.md                 generated: never edited
  <module>.py ...           the code the implementations name in `filepath`
  <code folder>/            a folder below it, with its own records when it holds code
  <sub-intent-id>/          a sub-intent beside its code: its own intent.csv and the same record files
```

## Where each record goes

| Record | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Implementation | The code folder of the file its `filepath` names (the nearest listed folder at or above it). |
| Solution | The lowest listed folder that holds the code of all its implementations, so its spec and code are in the same folder or one link apart. |
| Metric | With its solutions: the lowest listed folder that holds them all. |
| Problem | With its solutions, likewise. |
| Ideal | With its problems, likewise. |
| Intent | `intent.csv` in the top intent folder, or in a code folder that is a sub-intent (named by its `intent_id`). |
| A row with no code to follow | Stays in the top intent folder. |

A row never leaves the intent that owns it: the rows in and below a folder that holds an `intent.csv` belong to that sub-intent. `esoi records place` moves the records to these folders and `esoi records gather` moves them back.

## What an implementation points to

The `filepath` of an implementation names a source file in any language (code), a registry file that lists the files, services or practices that implement the solution (a reference), or `registry.csv::row-id` for a real-world system recorded as one row of a registry. See [forms of implementation](../../reference/records-beside-code.md#forms-of-implementation).

## The README of the folder

Written by `esoi readmes` from the records of the folder, never edited: for each solution its name, purpose, entry call and selected implementation and the files that implement it (from the records, the declarations and the ownership map); the diagram when the folders below it hold solutions it builds on; the implementations it holds, each with a link to its code; the metrics with their leaders; problems and ideals in a line each; and links up to the folder above or the intent, down to the folders below, and out to the repository's top README.
